nodes_add.name: Swami Niranjanananda Saraswati
nodes_add.note: Satyananda's successor; took over the running of the Bihar School of Yoga, Munger, in 1988. Birth year not verified in this batch.

nodes_add.name: Swami Akhandananda Saraswati (Mangrove Mountain)
nodes_add.note: Sent by Satyananda c. 1974 to oversee the Mangrove Mountain ashram, NSW; arrested 1989 on child sexual abuse charges, convicted and sentenced that year to 2 years 4 months (Royal Commission Case Study 21); served about 14 months before the High Court of Australia overturned the convictions on appeal in 1991 (Sky News, Dec 2014); died 1997. Distinct from other monks of the same name.

nodes_add.name: Bengali Baba (Swami Rama's guru)
nodes_add.note: Yogi from Bengal living in the Himalayan foothills who, by Swami Rama's own account, raised him; named in some accounts as Madhavananda Bharati. Known only from Swami Rama's testimony.

nodes_add.name: Pandit Rajmani Tigunait
nodes_add.note: Came to the US at Swami Rama's request; carried on the Himalayan Institute's work after 1996; author of At the Eleventh Hour (2001).

nodes_add.name: R. Sharath Jois
nodes_add.note: Grandson of Pattabhi Jois; director of KPJAYI; opened Sharath Yoga Centre 2019; Instagram statement 10 July 2019 acknowledging he witnessed improper adjustments; died 11 Nov 2024 in Virginia. Birth year derived from age 53 at death; confirm.

nodes_update.name: Swami Satyananda Saraswati
nodes_update.note: Born Almora 25 Dec 1923; Sivananda's disciple from 1943, sannyasa 12 Sept 1947; Bihar School of Yoga, Munger, 1963 (movement's date; others give 1964); yoga nidra; handed over to Niranjanananda 1988; Rikhia from Sept 1989; died there 5 Dec 2009.

nodes_update.name: Swami Rama
nodes_update.note: Born 1925 in Garhwal; US 1969; Menninger Foundation tests from March 1970; Himalayan Institute 1971 (Illinois), Honesdale PA 1977; HIHT Dehradun from 1989; died 13 Nov 1996. Civil jury verdict against the Institute, M.D. Pa., 4 Sept 1997.

nodes_update.name: K. Pattabhi Jois
nodes_update.note: Born Kowshika near Hassan 26 July 1915; Krishnamacharya's student from 1927; Ashtanga Yoga Research Institute, Mysore, 1948; died Mysore 18 May 2009.

edges_upsert.note: Came to the ashram 1943; sannyasa 12 September 1947; sent out 1956; Bihar School of Yoga, Munger, 1963 (movement's date; others give 1964).
Successor; took over the Bihar School of Yoga when Satyananda left Munger in 1988. Initiation year not verified.

Became his student the day after a demonstration at Jubilee Hall, Hassan, 1927; later studied with him in Mysore.
Grandson (son of Saraswathi Rangaswamy) and principal successor as teacher at the Mysore institute.
Swami Rama's own account in Living with the Himalayan Masters and the Institute's biography; teacher not otherwise documented.
Disciple; leads the Himalayan Institute after Swami Rama's death in 1996.

glossary.def: Yogic sleep. A guided practice done lying down, in which attention is led through the body, the breath and images while the practitioner stays aware at the edge of sleep; systematised by Swami Satyananda.
A resolve or intention. In yoga nidra, a short personal resolution repeated at the start and end of the practice.
Placing. A tantric rite in which mantras are placed, by touch or attention, on parts of the body.
Lock. A hatha yoga technique of contracting the throat, abdomen or pelvic floor to hold and direct the breath and energy.
Three places. In Ashtanga Vinyasa, the three points of attention held together in practice: breath, posture and gaze.
Gaze. A fixed point on which the eyes rest during a posture, used to steady attention.
A text, said to be by the sage Vamana, from which Krishnamacharya said he learned the vinyasa sequences; no copy has been examined and its existence is unverified.
